title: Active knight
objective: Take back a pawn while bringing a knight to an active square.

commentary_source.name: Uroschess original synthetic lesson
commentary_source.attribution: Original teaching text and practice position; not a historical game

steps.explanation: Black took White's d-pawn. Taking back can also improve a piece.
steps.detail: A knight in the centre can reach more squares than a knight at home.
steps.coach_prompt: Find a recapture that helps a piece grow stronger.

question.prompt: Which piece can take the pawn on d4 and reach the centre?
hints: Look at your knight on f3.
That knight can jump to d4.

tree.feedback: Your knight takes the pawn and stands in the centre, where it has more choices.
Black's knight on c6 can take your queen right away. Find a safer piece to take the pawn.

question.other_legal_move_text: That move may be useful, but the pawn on d4 is still there. Explore it, then try a recapture.

takeaway: Taking back can do two jobs: win a pawn and develop a piece.
